appraisal_events.evidence: planait sur Mlle Bloch la protection de M. Nissim Bernard... [les officiers] ne pouvaient en rien être utiles au directeur
appraisal_events.explanation: Although two officers formally complain about her public indiscretion, Mlle Bloch suffers no real consequence because M. Nissim Bernard's daily, lucrative presence at the hotel gives him informal sway over the directeur that outweighs the officers' one-night stay.

appraisal_events.evidence: aucune invitation n'aurait pu le détourner de rentrer dîner dans son chez lui... Mais jamais il ne déjeunait chez lui... les quarante années qui séparaient M. Nissim Bernard du jeune commis auraient dû préserver celui-ci d'un contact peu aimable
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator ironically contrasts Nissim Bernard's ostentatious performance of family devotion (never missing dinner with his nephew) with his actual daily habit of lunching at the hotel to see a young employee, implying a compromising private life beneath the respectable façade.

status_effects.explanation: She remains shielded and effectively included at the hotel despite conduct that drew a formal complaint, because of the protective leverage attached to her association with Nissim Bernard.
The exposed gap between his loudly performed family virtue and his actual daily habits locally lowers how the narrator presents him, even as his practical influence remains real.

ambiguities: The passage breaks off mid-quotation from Racine, so the full implication of M. Nissim Bernard's relationship with the young commis is only suggested rather than fully stated, which tempers confidence in reading E2 as a clear diminishment rather than mere ironic scene-setting.
